predecessors.note: The northern provinces under the governor of Quito.

land.text: the north under Atahualpa: the Quito highlands and Tumebamba

successors.note: The faction wins and its ruler is the Sapa Inca from April 1532.

capitals.name: Quito
capitals.note: 'Atahualpa gathered the northern army in Quito'; the Atahualpa page has him in Cajamarca with about 80,000 men when the Spanish approached (undated) while his generals fought. Coordinates are the gazetteer's.

rulers.name: Atahualpa (Atawallpa)
rulers.title: claimant, governor of Quito
rulers.note: Governor of Quito under Huáscar; Sapa Inca from April 1532 (Atahualpa page).

correction.text: the north under Atahualpa: the Quito highlands and Tumebamba

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1529-1532: 'Atahualpa controlled the north (Quito and the northern campaign), and Huáscar held Cusco and the south'; Atahualpa 'gathered the northern army in Quito' and Tumebamba is where Huáscar's army surprised him. The page gives no frontier; the Quito highlands and a disc round Tumebamba (Cuenca) stand for the north.

region.text: the north under Atahualpa: the Quito highlands and Tumebamba

ledger.note: 1529: Atahualpa makes war on Huáscar from Quito. The Inca Civil War 'began in 1529, and lasted until 1532'; Huáscar, crowned at Cusco, had Atahualpa's messengers killed and sent his captains back dressed as women, so 'Atahualpa then declared war'. Atahualpa page: Huáscar had appointed him governor of Quito; by 1529 relations 'had quite deteriorated'.

region.text: the north under Atahualpa: the Quito highlands and Tumebamba

ledger.note: 1529: the north follows Atahualpa. The Quito highlands and Tumebamba (with Cañari support Huáscar's army struck there) are held by Atahualpa's faction.

region.text: the highland band from Tumebamba to Cusco where the armies fought

ledger.note: 1529: the armies of Atahualpa and Huáscar fight across the highlands. Battles on the page, undated except Quipaipan: Tumebamba, Ambato, Bonbon, Jauja, Pincos, Andaguaylas, Limatambo, Ichubamba, Vilcas.

region.text: the highland band from Tumebamba to Cusco where the armies fought

ledger.note: April 1532: Atahualpa wins at Quipaipán. The Atahualpa page dates the battles of Mullihambato, Chimborazo and Quipaipán to April 1532; Quizquiz and Chalcuchímac defeated Huáscar at Quipaipán, captured him and seized Cusco (infobox: the war ends April 1532).

region.text: the north under Atahualpa: the Quito highlands and Tumebamba

ledger.note: April 1532: the north returns to the single Inca state under Atahualpa; he reigned from April 1532 (Atahualpa page).

region.text: the north under Atahualpa: the Quito highlands and Tumebamba

ledger.note: April 1532: Atahualpa's faction becomes the Inca state. 'He reigned from April 1532 until his capture and execution'; the Inca Empire infobox lists Atahualpa as Sapa Inca 1532-1533.

region.text: the north under Atahualpa: the Quito highlands and Tumebamba

ledger.note: April 1532: the rebellion ends in victory and its land is the Inca Empire's.

wars.name: Inca Civil War

zones.text: the highland band from Tumebamba to Cusco where the armies fought

wars.outcome: Atahualpa's northern army defeats Huáscar's; Huáscar captured, Cusco seized by Quizquiz; Atahualpa rules the empire from April 1532. The war helped the Spanish conquest.
wars.note: Battle dates: only the April 1532 group (Mullihambato, Chimborazo, Quipaipán) is dated, by the Atahualpa page; the Civil War page puts Quipaipan in January 1532 and ends the war in April 1532 in its infobox.

certainty.note: No frontier on either page; battles are named places.

sources.title: Inca Civil War
sources.note: 1529-1532 (infobox April 1532), Atahualpa at Quito vs Huáscar at Cusco, battles, Quipaipan, outcome.

sources.title: Atahualpa
sources.note: Governor of Quito, civil war 1529-1532, battles of Mullihambato, Chimborazo and Quipaipán in April 1532, reign April 1532-July 1533, Cajamarca, Quito's independence contested.

notes: A rebel entity per master-plan rule 5, written because the group scope asks for the civil war as a contest. Both sides are the Inca state; Atahualpa won, so the faction merges into inca-empire in April 1532. The extent of the north is a reading of 'Quito and the northern campaign' (the Inca Civil War page does not use the term Chinchaysuyu). The Atahualpa page says Quito's status as an independent kingdom 'rests on sources the page describes as unconfirmed' and that Atahualpa sought an independent state there: no Kingdom of Quito dossier is written. Dates conflict on Huayna Capac's death (about 1525 or 1527) and on Atahualpa's execution (26 July 1533 in the body, 29 August in the lead of the Atahualpa page, 29 August on the Civil War and Spanish conquest pages). The Chimborazo battle is on the Atahualpa page (April 1532), not on the Civil War page.
